text:
devon: Heads-up — found a customer hit where an old feature-flag value leaked into routing policies after a config import. We need a short playbook for phased enforcement + handling stale configs. Ideas?

sarah: ugh. can you paste the diff? is this the `route_by_region` flag thing?

mike: +1 to getting a checklist. high-level: detect stale -> warn in console + api -> soft-enforce (telemetry-gated) -> hard-enforce with killswitch.

devon: exact payload: after import we had `route_by_region: true` in a subset of accounts while org-level default was false. the runtime honored the per-account value even though capacity rules assumed org-level. caused request routing to wrong pool.

jess: concrete proposal: 1) add a `stale_since` tag to the config metadata when source != canonical. 2) Console shows a yellow banner on flag pages for flagged accounts. 3) API returns `flag_state: STALE` with 200 but telemetry events emitted.

ops-bot: Incident detected: config-mismatch on 12 accounts. Alerting on >5% mismatch rate.

devon: I like metric gating. we should avoid surprise hard rollouts. What should the telemetry thresholds be?

mike: threshold idea: 0.5% error delta -> warn, 2% -> soft-enforce (route fallback but keep logs), 5% -> page + escalate, 10%+ -> auto-mitigate (fallback to org default). numbers adjustable per-customer tier.

jess: soft-enforce = runtime applies `fallback_policy: ORG_DEFAULT` but still records original decision and emits `routing_override` event with tags. hard-enforce = mutate the stored per-account config to org default (requires audit entry).

devon: mutating stored config worries me from an audit/security POV. prefer a runtime-only enforcement, then send a DRI email for manual commit.

console-team: UI notes: show a timeline on the flag page: source -> detected_stale_ts -> soft-enforce_ts -> suggested_action. Add quick action buttons: `Mark canonical`, `Request rollback`, `Open incident`.

mike: also need an API change: config GET should include `canonical_source` and `detected_diff_hash` so automated tooling can compare. example: `GET /v1/configs/{id}` returns `{"value":..., "canonical_source":"org:default", "diff_hash":"abc123"}`

devon: can we gate soft-enforce behind a runtime flag so we can experiment with a small % of traffic? like a phased enforcement rollout?

jess: yes — introduce `enforcement_window_pct` in the enforcement policy. runtime will sample by request ID and apply fallback if within pct. default 0 -> 100.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: config-service v3.14 will add `detected_stale` and `enforcement_window_pct` fields. 2023-11-02 03:00 UTC.

devon: steps for rollout plan (draft):
- bake telemetry and alerts in staging (generate mismatches)
- deploy fields to prod read-only (no enforcement) for 24h
- enable UI warnings and events for 48h
- enable soft-enforce with enforcement_window_pct=10 for 2h, monitor
- bump to 50% if no regressions for 6h
- 100% soft-enforce + notify DRI
- offer manual mutation after confirmation

mike: add automated rollback criteria: increase in latency > 5% or routing error rate > 1% in the affected shard for 10m -> rollback to previous enforcement_window_pct.

jess: snippet for enforcement policy (draft):
```
{ "policy_name": "stale_config_enforce_v1",
  "detection": {"source_mismatch": true},
  "enforcement": {"mode":"soft", "enforcement_window_pct": 10, "fallback":"org_default"},
  "telemetry_hooks": ["routing_override","stale_detected"]
}
```
devon: ops question — how do we ensure the console quick-actions are permissioned? only infra-admin + account-owner should be able to mutate or mark canonical.

console-team: permissions: use existing RBAC roles. add `config:mutate` and `config:mark_canonical` scopes. show disabled buttons if user lacks perms with tooltip explaining who can act.

mike: on the SDK/API side, add idempotency token to any mutation and require `reason` field for audit logs. Also background job to create a PR-like review item when someone requests mutation.

devon: agree. also we need a migration path for cached configs in edge proxies. They may carry stale values in memory. plan: send `invalidate_cache` events to proxies when we detect stale + on soft-enforce start. proxies should support `grace_ttl` so they can finish in-flight requests but drop after 30s.

jess: QA checklist idea: 1) simulate import with conflicting sources, 2) observe `stale_detected` events, 3) check UI banner appears, 4) enable 10% enforcement, 5) validate `routing_override` telemetry, 6) validate proxy cache invalidation works.

devon: can someone own writing the playbook doc and the runbook for on-call?

mike: I can draft the runbook (ops steps, rollback criteria, dashboard links).

jess: I'll draft the console and API spec and a sample payloads page.

console-team: we'll add the banner + quick actions prototype to the design board, ping when you need assets.

devon: thanks. put PRs into `platform/config-enforcement` and mark them `WIP`. I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: config-service v3.14 -> staging. Commit 9a7f3e.

mike: small follow-up: let's include a `stale_score` in telemetry (0-100) so we can rank by seriousness and auto-prioritize.

jess: SGTM. use hash-diff + last-update-age to compute score.

devon: perfect. end state: no silent hard-mutations, clear UI + telemetry, RBAC for actions, phased enforcement % with rollback gates, proxy invalidation. Good first pass.

mike: will add dashboard panels: stale_count by org, stale_rate over time, enforcement_window_pct heatmap, latency delta when enforcement tripped.

devon: ok closing thread — thanks all. put links to PRs in #eng-releases when ready.
